newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks recoup losses, end barely changed.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks recoup losses, end barely changed.

text.p: Australian shares ended Tuesday barely changed from Monday's record levels, as the strong underlying sentiment won over an early bout of profit-taking on the first day of the new financial year.

"We had a very weak morning, and it was a good recovery to claw back all those early losses. It's a tricky time of year with a lot of book-squaring and people trying to take home profits," one Brisbane-based dealer said.
The All Ordinaries index closed 4.7 points lower at 2721.2, down from a record close of 2725.9 on Monday. Turnover reached a healthy A$854.4 million.

The Hong Kong handover had no impact on the Australian share market, dealers said, with most eyes on the upcoming two-day U.S. Federal Open Market Committe meeting and the outcome of Reserve Bank of Australia's monthly meeting earlier on Tuesday.
"I think some still hope for a (domestic) rate cut, but the chances have diminished," one dealer said.
The banking sector initially slumped in disappointment as no cut was announced this morning, but later recovered some losses to end 0.37 percent lower on the day.
Commonwealth Bank fell 16 cents to A$15.84, and Westpac Banking six cents to A$7.91, while National Australia Bank recovered completely to end 4.9 cents higher at A$19.019.
Profit-taking pulled down Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd in the early hours, but optimism over the giant's future earnings reversed losses. The stock ended 3.7 cents up at A$19.52.
Other blue chips were mixed, with miners Rio Tinto, down 11 cents to A$22.47 and WMC one cent up at A$8.36.
Among the winners were News Corp shares, which rose 12 cents to A$6.47 after its ADRs firmed in New York overnight.

News that Coca-Cola Amatil shareholders had approved a share-swap deal with San Miguel of the Philippines was already discounted and went by barely noticed. The stock fell 30 cents to A$16.90 after a 52 cent rise on Monday.
Casino operator Crown Ltd ended five cents higher at A$2.18 with almost 22 million shares traded.
Software systems group Computershare jumped 95 cents to A$9.45 in modest volume after it said it had placed 2.29 million shares with The Royal Bank of Scotland Plc.
